prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Full SCENE STATE SHEET for a physical Mars expedition game. Match the supplied realistic painterly cream-and-teal machinery, ochre landscape, restrained cobalt science equipment, mustard rover fittings. Locally made parts are simple cut straight steel and bolted joints, never elaborate molded industrial machinery. Factory precision parts are imported. No people, text, numerals, labels, captions, borders, arrows, diagrams or UI. Each panel repeats EXACTLY the same camera, framing, object positions, light, room/landscape and perspective, changing ONLY the specified state. Every recurring object is the same actual object. Frame the full installation in the upper two thirds; lower third is quiet natural floor or ground for the movable inventory. No loose decorative objects. Whole scenes will be cropped into registered fixed targets; keep independent working regions clearly separated. Square panels, not portrait strips.
Layout: 3 columns by 1 rows of equal SQUARE scenes. Reading order left to right then next row. Return to the SAME outdoor round habitat, actual deployed solar array and plugged-in atmospheric processor from reference1 FINAL panel. Same camera and positions. Habitat has its original clamped pressure patch, high dish remains mounted. Exterior station inlet is beside array route, not inside. Storm has passed; daylight returns.
STATE 1: Installed solar panels coated with reddish dust, visibly dull. Their feeder connection is safely UNPLUGGED at the array end; the habitat-side inlet exists. Do not remove the array from its bolted supports.
STATE 2: Same panels now brushed clean with dark reflective photovoltaic faces. The array feed remains unplugged. Same installed processor and dish.
STATE 3: Same cleaned panels, now connected by their actual feeder lead to the habitat inlet. Modest power indicator lit. No duplicate array or portable panel token.
